root_cause.text: The `sctp_getsockopt_peer_auth_chunks` function in the SCTP subsystem performs an insufficient buffer size validation that omits the `struct sctp_authchunks` header size, allowing `copy_to_user` to write beyond the user-supplied buffer boundary.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the validation condition in `net/sctp/socket.c` from `if (len < num_chunks)` to `if (len < sizeof(struct sctp_authchunks) + num_chunks)`, aligning with the CVE description that the original check was "missing the sizeof(struct sctp_authchunks) = 8-byte header" which caused `copy_to_user()` to write 8 bytes past the declared buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This buffer size validation at line 7036 only checks against sizeof(struct sctp_authchunks) header size but fails to account for the additional data payload (num_chunks * sizeof(__u16)) that will be written by copy_to_user, allowing writes beyond the user-supplied buffer boundary.

The copy_to_user operation on line 7040 copies peer authentication chunk data without verifying that the remaining buffer space accounts for both the header and all chunk data, enabling out-of-bounds writes when combined with the insufficient validation above.
